localised_description: Every ridge above the valley carries its own wall, and the people go up to it with the herds. An army that takes the valley has taken nothing.
The iron of the twelve states goes north to the commanderies, east to Ye and over the water to Wa, and is weighed out as money. What stays here is worn.
Men who follow sable and tiger through the eastern hills, and who make the sandalwood bow, do not lose their way nor miss their mark.
Gifts carried to the commandery at Lelang buy silk, seals of office, and the years we need to make ready.
The pole is raised with its bells and drums, and inside the sodo no man may be seized. The people keep faith with the cheon'gun, and so with you.
In Buyeo a thief repays twelve times what he took, and his household with him. Word of it travels further than any magistrate.
Gyeru, Sono, Jeolo, Sunno and Gwanno. The king rules with the five bu at his shoulder, and the levies come in on time.
The grain he lent out in the famine year is standing in the line with him now, and it does not break.
A minister who has broken ground with his own hands knows exactly how long men can be asked to stand.
She moved once, in the dark, before anyone knew there was a decision to be made. She picks her man and she does not raise her voice.
The throne passed him by, so he went to Liaodong for thirty thousand men and came back to argue the point.
He put his capital behind a mountain wall. Whatever comes up the slope arrives with nothing left in it.
Forty years of raids across the Silla border. His men have stopped asking what the quarrel was about.
He led his father's armies against the Malgal long before the crown came to him. The veterans know the voice.
He is said to read flood and drought a season out. A battlefield holds nothing like that much weather.
When the call came from the south the column was on the road before the envoy had eaten.
Every ingot that leaves the Nakdong passes a wharf he owns, and the best of it never leaves at all.
She came ashore with a stone pagoda in the hold. Men who fight under her expect to be on the winning side.
The first king came out of an egg. The second has to be a government, and the ranks can feel the difference.
Burn the valley, drive in the herds and hold the ridge wall. Let them come to us, and let them find nothing on the way.
Sworn at the tenth-month rite before heaven and the ancestors of the five bu. Men who have sworn together do not give ground.
The horse clans of the northern plain ride down whatever stands in front of them, and think about their own guard afterwards.
The horse clan answers for the herds, as the ox, pig and dog clans answer for theirs. Buyeo horses are known as far as Luoyang.
The ring-pommel sword is made to cut, not to parry. Shrug the plate off your shoulders and use it.
Byeonhan iron goes out to the commanderies, to Ye and to Wa as money. What stays at home is worn.
The bow of the Maek is asked for by name in the Han markets. Every archer in the army draws it at once.
The sandalwood bow of Ye, cut and cured in the eastern hills, outranges what the commanderies issue.
The pole is raised with its bells and drums. Inside the sodo no man may be seized and no man takes a step back - nor a step forward.
Sowing in the fifth month, harvest in the tenth: dozens stamping in time, and the drums never out of earshot.
